description: Build the Python dictionary generator tool in tools/dictionary-generator/. This is a standalone, maintainer-run CLI (NOT part of the C++/MSVC build or CI). It fetches GW2 data from the official REST API (api.guildwars2.com/v2), translates EN->PT-BR offline via Argos Translate (Opcao C: free, no API key, no limits), and writes dictionaries in the exact JSON schema the Bronco C++ loader expects. Must be idempotent, resumable, rate-limited, with retry/backoff and a progress bar. Fetching and translation must be decoupled so raw English data can be produced even without the Argos model installed.
steps: Create tools/dictionary-generator/requirements.txt pinning: requests, tqdm, argostranslate. Add a short comment that argostranslate pulls heavy transitive deps (ctranslate2, sentencepiece, stanza) and downloads a ~100MB+ en->pt model at runtime.

Create tools/dictionary-generator/gw2_api.py: a fetch layer. Functions to (a) GET the full id list from an endpoint (/v2/<endpoint>), (b) fetch details in batches of at most 200 ids via /v2/<endpoint>?ids=...&lang=en, extracting 'name' and 'description'. Implement rate limiting (throttle to stay under ~300 requests/min, e.g. a configurable min delay ~0.25s between requests), retry with exponential backoff on HTTP 429/5xx and connection errors (honor Retry-After when present), and a requests.Session. Cache raw EN batches to disk under tools/dictionary-generator/cache/raw/<endpoint>/ so re-runs resume from cache instead of re-downloading. Endpoints to support: skills, items, traits, specializations, professions, pets, masteries.

Create tools/dictionary-generator/translator.py: an offline translation layer wrapping Argos Translate. On demand, ensure the en->pt language package is installed (download+install via argostranslate.package if missing) exposed through an --install-model action. Provide translate(text) that returns the PT-BR string. Persist a translation cache (JSON keyed by source English string) under tools/dictionary-generator/cache/translations.json so repeated terms are not re-translated and runs are resumable. Import argostranslate lazily inside functions so the module can be imported (and fetch-only / dry-run modes can run) even when Argos is not installed; raise a clear, actionable error only when translation is actually attempted without the model.

Create tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py: the main CLI. Args: --category {skills,items,traits,specializations,professions,pets,masteries,all}, --limit N (cap ids for sampling), --lang-pkg en->pt handling via --install-model, --output-dir (default data/dictionaries/pt-br), --min-delay, --no-translate (produce entries with en only / passthrough for structure demo), --dry-run (offline: run internal self-checks without network or Argos). Pipeline per category: fetch id list -> fetch details in batches (cached) -> for each unique English name (and optionally description) translate to PT-BR (cached) -> build the dictionary dict -> write JSON. Deduplicate by normalized (lowercased) English key to match C++ case-insensitive lookup, skipping empty names. Show a tqdm progress bar over batches/entries. Map category to output filename: skills->skills.json, items->items.json, traits->traits.json (and reasonable filenames for the others). Print a summary (counts fetched/translated/written, cache hits).

Ensure the generated JSON has EXACTLY the schema the C++ loader consumes: top-level {"locale": "pt-br", "category": <category>, "version": "1.0.0", "entries": [ {"en": <English>, "translated": <PT-BR>} ]}. Write UTF-8 with ensure_ascii=false and 4-space indentation to match existing files in data/dictionaries/pt-br/.

Add built-in offline self-checks (invoked by --dry-run) that require neither network nor Argos: (a) build a dictionary dict from a small in-memory sample and assert the schema (keys present, entries is a list, each entry has non-empty 'en' and 'translated'); (b) round-trip the translation cache save/load; (c) verify id-list batching splits into chunks of <=200 and reassembles without loss; (d) verify normalized-key dedup drops case-duplicate English names. Exit non-zero if any check fails.

Create tools/dictionary-generator/README.md (in Brazilian Portuguese) documenting: purpose, that it uses the official GW2 REST API (explicitly permitted by ArenaNet 'Paineis que consomem a API REST oficial via chave publica'), Opcao C offline Argos model, setup (venv + pip install -r requirements.txt + --install-model), usage examples for sampling and full runs, that it is idempotent/resumable via the cache, expected runtime (items ~90k ids is long-running / can take hours; skills ~few thousand), disk needs (raw cache + Argos model ~hundreds of MB), memory needs, that it does NOT run in CI, and how the output plugs into data/dictionaries/pt-br/. Cross-link from docs/ADDING_LANGUAGES.md is optional.
Update .gitignore to ignore tools/dictionary-generator/cache/ (raw API cache, translation cache, Argos model downloads) so large/generated artifacts are not committed.
acceptance_criteria: tools/dictionary-generator/ contains generate_dictionaries.py, gw2_api.py, translator.py, requirements.txt, and README.md.
python3 -m py_compile on all .py files in tools/dictionary-generator/ succeeds.
python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --dry-run runs offline (no network, no Argos) and exits 0 with all self-checks passing.
Importing translator.py does NOT require argostranslate to be installed (lazy import); translation only fails with a clear error when actually attempted without the model.

The dictionary builder emits JSON with top-level locale/category/version/entries and each entry having string 'en' and 'translated' keys, byte-compatible with src/translation/dictionary.cpp expectations.
README.md is written in Brazilian Portuguese and documents setup, usage, resumability, runtime, disk/memory, and CI exclusion.
verification: Run: python3 tools/dictionary-generator/generate_dictionaries.py --dry-run  and confirm exit code 0 and self-checks pass
Run: python3 -c 'import tools' is NOT expected; instead confirm 'import translator' style modules import without argostranslate by temporarily checking the lazy-import path (documented in README).
Manually inspect a builder-produced JSON snippet (from --dry-run or --no-translate small sample) and confirm schema matches data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json
findings: Implemented the standalone Python tool under tools/dictionary-generator/ (gw2_api.py, translator.py, generate_dictionaries.py, requirements.txt, README.md in PT-BR) and added tools/dictionary-generator/cache/ to .gitignore. Opcao C (Argos Translate offline) as confirmed 3x by the user; live steering messages during work re-confirmed Opcao C and rejected the Google Translate/SQLite alternative, so no change of direction. Decoupling: BOTH argostranslate AND requests are imported lazily. In this sandbox neither requests nor argostranslate is installed, so a top-level `import requests` in gw2_api.py would have broken --dry-run; made requests lazy via _get_requests() so the fetch module imports offline and only errors when a network call is actually made. Verification all green: (1) py_compile on all 3 .py files OK; (2) `--dry-run` exits 0 with all 5 offline self-checks passing (schema build, translation-cache UTF-8 round-trip, <=200 batching split/reassemble, normalized-key dedup, lazy Translator construction) using NO network and NO Argos; (3) translator.py imports and Translator() constructs without argostranslate installed, raising a clear TranslationError only when translate() is actually called; (4) builder-produced JSON validated to match data/dictionaries/pt-br/skills.json schema (locale=pt-br, category, version=1.0.0, entries[] with non-empty string en+translated), UTF-8 (non-ASCII preserved) with 4-space indent. Note: generated entry objects are multi-line (standard json.dump indent=4) vs the existing hand-written single-line entries; the C++ nlohmann::json loader parses both identically, so this is schema/byte-compatible for the loader. Did NOT run a live fetch (FEAT-002 handles the demonstration run); did not modify any C++ code. Did not commit task-state changes to other tasks.
